transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Alder ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (Alder Platform Eng), Lena Wu (Alder Security)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're running about 55 minutes, agenda is quick onboarding check, infra access, benchmark review, and next steps.
[00:20] Priya: Thanks Maya, quick note, Priya here — happy to kick off with status, we completed the initial data prep and we've been running local evals, got some noisy results but overall okay.
[01:05] Daniel: Great, can you remind us which model variant you're using for the tests? Is it the 13B or did you switch to a 7B quantized?
[01:18] Priya: We're on the 13b fp16 baseline, but we've tried a couple 8-bit runs locally, that's the noisy part, latency is fine but quality dips on long contexts.
[01:42] Tom: On the infra side, we still haven't got the kubeconfig or the peering completed, we raised the ticket last week but need the exact IP ranges from Redwood.
[02:10] Maya: Right, Tom — we sent a runbook draft yesterday, I'll resend with explicit CIDR ranges and a step-by-step. There was a small mismatch in the peering instructions — apologies, will clarify.
[02:55] Lena: From security perspective, SOC2 is okay but we need to confirm KMS integration and data retention defaults for the pilot. Can you share the compliance doc?
[03:20] Maya: Yep, I'll attach the compliance pack after the call. It has SOC2, PCI notes, and a note about our optional customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
[04:05] Daniel: Jumping into benchmarks — we ran Redwood-hosted baseline tests for Alder's prompts. The CSV we have includes p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and example failure modes. We saw higher p95 on long token windows due to KV cache misses in our config.
[04:38] Priya: Could be the prompt shaping, we have a lot of system messages and repeated prefixes. Any suggestions to preserve cache friendliness?
[05:00] Daniel: Two quick tips — reduce repeated system prefixes, use shorter instruction templates, and enable prefix KV cache in the runtime config. We'll share a recommended batching/kvcfg. Also consider quantization tradeoffs: 4-bit reduces memory but needs per-task eval.
[05:33] Priya: Got it. The local 8-bit runs were more memory efficient but we saw hallucinations on multi-turn.
[05:50] Daniel: Yeah that's expected, depending on temperature and prompt. We'll give a config with tuned temperature, top-p, and cache params.
[06:20] Tom: Back to access — we need an access window for our cluster — can Redwood support short-lived certs or do you only do static kubeconfigs?
[06:40] Maya: For Dedicated pilot we can support both. For Private deployment we can do short-lived certs and customer-managed KMS options. For the current hosted evaluation, a service account + kubeconfig with IP allowlist is typical.
[07:05] Lena: Also need to confirm audit logs retention and whether token-level traces have redaction defaults. We prefer PII redaction on sample traces.
[07:28] Daniel: By default we redact PII in traces, but we can enable full traces with customer permission; audit logs retention is configurable per plan. We'll include that in the compliance pack.
[08:00] Priya: Any rough timeline for enabling peering? If we give the network team the CIDR today, how long?
[08:15] Tom: Depends on approval cycle, but usually 2-3 business days if no changes.
[08:30] Maya: We'll aim to have runbook + CIDR by EOD today. That gets Tom unblocked.
[09:00] Daniel: Quick note on perf numbers — for your batch of prompts (avg 320 tokens), we saw p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 480ms on Redwood-hosted 13B fp16. Quantized tests were ~20-30% cheaper but p95 increased. We left detailed per-prompt breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[09:45] Priya: Can you push that spreadsheet to the shared drive? Our ML team will compare to local runs.
[10:00] Maya: Yes, I'll upload the CSV and link in Slack, and I'll include a short commentary on the interesting prompt shapes.
[10:30] Tom: One more infra question — the pilot will likely want Dedicated reserved capacity if latency stabilizes. Can you provide ballpark pricing for a 3-node Dedicated pool?
[10:55] Maya: We can — I'll prepare a preliminary sizing and pricing note. For a 3-GPU pool with autoscale buffer, approximate monthly commit is in the deck range. I'll send a ballpark by Friday.
[11:30] Lena: From compliance, we might need a subset of pilot logs to be stored in our S3 with CMEK keys. Is that supported?
[11:50] Daniel: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed encryption keys and S3 sinks with access controls. We'll outline the exact steps.
[12:20] Priya: Great. On tuning — do you recommend changing sequence length or truncating? We have several long customer messages.
[12:40] Daniel: Best practice is to chunk long contexts, keep the most relevant recent history, and use retrieval augmentation for older context. Also set KV cache to persist across requests when safe. We'll include examples.
[13:10] Tom: Any blockers on your side for running the deeper perf tests we proposed? We asked for a small private dataset and test harness access.
[13:30] Maya: We just need the dataset access and service account; once we have that, Daniel can run the tests and share results within 48 hours.
[14:00] Priya: We'll grant a read-only S3 role and send sample prompts.
[14:20] Maya: Perfect.
[14:40] Daniel: One small transcription note — earlier I mentioned KV cache misses, spelled K-V cache — sometimes transcript converts to 'cue-v cache' so apologies for any typos in the doc.
[15:05] Priya: (laughs) noted.
[15:25] Maya: OK let's recap: action items are Maya sends runbook & CIDR today, Daniel shares benchmark CSV & tuning config by Friday, Alder team to grant peering/kubeconfig access, Lena confirms compliance answers. We'll also schedule infra handoff next Wednesday.
[15:55] Tom: Works for us.
[16:10] Lena: One last question — will Redwood provide a 1:1 SE hours for the pilot run?
[16:25] Maya: Yes, our pilot includes SE time for the initial onboarding and tuning, we'll list hours in the sizing note.
[16:40] Priya: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[16:55] Maya: Thanks all, I'll follow up in Slack and attach the artifacts.
[17:05] [meeting end]
